description: Search everything The Living Bread holds with one query and get back a flat list of short results with ids, for the search-then-fetch pattern of connector clients (ChatGPT deep research and similar): a Bible reference, a matching need's verse set, sourced entities, churches and gatherings within 250 km when the query is a place, and communities whose name or description contains a query word. query is tried in order as a Bible reference, a need, an entity question, a place (only when it is not a reference or need), and community words. Then call fetch with an id to read it in full. When you want a direct answer rather than a list, use ask_living_bread; for verses by wording use scripture_search. Never empty: with no match it returns one result linking to the home page. The query (no user id) is logged anonymously. Access: no sign-in; shared limit of 300 requests a minute per IP.

query.description: Free text, 1 to 300 characters: a reference ("Psalm 23"), a need ("anxiety"), a name ("Augustine"), a place ("Lagos"), or a topic.

name: search

attribution.description: Credit line for the data: The Living Bread (living-bread.org).

content_layers.description: Which fields are Scripture and which are human interpretation or reflection.

evidence.description: Present when Scripture was read: translation, canon, corpus version, attribution, and a SHA-256 per passage.

freshness.description: How current the answer is: kind (scheduled | recently_observed | verified_live | record), retrieved_at, available_now (true only when activity was verified live).

ids.description: Up to 25 ids found in this answer, for follow-up calls.

license.description: License URL of the returned data (CC BY 4.0 unless stated).

next_actions.description: Up to 4 links the person can open next.

ok.description: Always true on a successful answer (errors come back as isError, never here).

result_state.description: "empty" when nothing matched (count 0, no results); the text then says so plainly.

results.description: Matches with id (verse:<ref>, need:<slug>, church:<uuid>, gathering:<uuid>, community:<uuid>, or an lb: id), title, one-line text and a web URL. Pass id to fetch.

source_url.description: The first public web page this answer came from or points to.

visibility.description: "public" for shared data, "yours" for the signed-in believer's own data.

title: Search The Living Bread
